acceptanceCriteria: A repository script (or documented wrapper) admits `go test` / `go build ./...` through a host-wide counting lock with a configurable limit and bounded `-p`.
Lane charters use the wrapper for every heavy Go command.
Measured: with 5 concurrent lanes, a representative focused package test's wall time is within 1.5x of its quiet-host time, or the remaining gap is recorded.
body: Evidence: owner-requested audit on 2026-10-17 of orchestrator session 03e2afac (Handoff 2026-10-14): 206 Claude Code lane subagents, 374 lane-hours over 77 h wall. Measured from subagent transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/-Users-russelllewis-projects-corvint/03e2afac-.../subagents (tool_use to tool_result timestamps) and live host reads. Toolchain: corvint-tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.615, Go 1.27.2, macOS 12-core/64 GB host. Lanes ran go test 2,464 times for 90.9 h total; there were 166 go test commands over 10 min (28.2 h). Each lane runs `go test -count=1` independently, so 5-7 lanes overlap Go builds and test binaries on 12 cores. Expected: heavy test and build commands across lanes are admitted through one host-wide counting lock (about 2 heavy runs at once, `-p` bounded per run), so each run finishes in its quiet-host time. Related: V1-1550/V1-1573 capacity slots cover Tasks pool acquire, not ad-hoc lane test commands.
title: Concurrent lanes need a shared host test semaphore so go test runs queue instead of thrashing
